festivals: Mahashivaratri (night-long jagran; Shivling decorated with Rudraksha)
Sawan Mondays (grand fair; Shiv Parikrama of Agra; devotees offer water on the Shivling)

history.summary: Balkeshwar Mahadev Temple, on the banks of the Yamuna at Balkeshwar Ghat in Agra, is one of the four Shiva temples traditionally located at the four corners of Agra (along with Mankameshwar, Kaileshwar and Teeleshwar Nath). Its ancient name was Bilvakeshwar Mahadev Temple: local belief holds that some 600-700 years ago, when a dense forest of Bael (Bilva) trees was cleared, a self-manifested (Swayambhu) Shivling was discovered here, and the shrine took its name from the Bilva forest. Shiva is fond of Bael leaves, so Bael leaves are traditionally offered on the Shivling. The Shivling is anointed with sandalwood and saffron, which are distributed to devotees as prasad. On Mahashivaratri the Shivling is decorated with Rudraksha and a night-long jagran is held by the Yamuna; on Mondays of the Sawan month a grand fair is organised and the temple is part of Agra's traditional Shiv Parikrama, during which devotees offer water on the Shivling. The temple complex, spread over about an acre, has a simple traditional Hindu temple style with a garbhagriha, open courtyard, carved walls and a small dome.

name: Balkeshwar Mahadev Temple
town_description: Agra, in western Uttar Pradesh on the banks of the Yamuna, is world-famous for the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri. Balkeshwar is a northern locality of the city, known for the Balkeshwar Ghat on the Yamuna, the temple, and the nearby Kailash Nagar and Kamla Nagar areas. Other Yamuna-bank Shiva shrines such as Kaila Devi Temple and Teeleshwar Nath Mahadev (Parvati Ghat) are close by.

travel.airport: Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyay Airport, Agra (Kheria) (approx. 13-17 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Agra Cantt and Agra Fort stations (roughly 6-10 km from the temple; local buses, autos and taxis available).
travel.road: Easily reachable within Agra city by local buses, auto-rickshaws and taxis; about 1.5 km from the Water Works area on the Yamuna bank.

visitor_information.best_time: March to October is suggested by local guides, with the Sawan month (July-August) being the most devotional time thanks to the Monday fairs; October-March has Agra's pleasant winter weather. Abhishek is best attended before 7 AM.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 6:00 AM to 12:30 PM; evening 4:00 PM to 10:00 PM, open all days. Extended crowds and night-long jagran on Mahashivaratri and Sawan Mondays.
